steps.action:
# The Capital of Australia: Canberra

The capital of Australia is **Canberra**. Below is an in-depth exploration of this answer.

---

## Why Canberra — Not Sydney or Melbourne?

A very common misconception (even among some Australians) is that Sydney is the capital. In fact, Sydney is the largest city, but it is *not* the capital. The reason Canberra exists as a purpose-built capital comes down to colonial rivalry.

When Australia federated on **January 1, 1901**, uniting six former British colonies into the Commonwealth of Australia, two cities competed fiercely to be the national capital:

- **Sydney** — oldest, largest, capital of New South Wales (NSW)
- **Melbourne** — second-largest, capital of Victoria

Neither would concede to the other. The compromise embedded in **Section 125 of the Australian Constitution** was:

1. The capital must be located **within New South Wales**
2. But **at least 100 miles (≈160 km) from Sydney**
3. **Melbourne** would serve as the *temporary* seat of government in the meantime

This elegant political solution meant that both sides got something — and neither got everything.

---

## Selecting the Site

Several sites across southern NSW were considered. After years of surveys and debate, in **1908** the federal government selected the **Yass-Canberra district** in a high tableland region. The land was ceded from NSW to the Commonwealth, becoming the **Australian Capital Territory (ACT)**.

---

## The Name "Canberra"

The name is widely believed to derive from an **Aboriginal Ngunnawal word** — often cited as meaning **"meeting place."** Some sources trace it to "Kamberra" or "Canberry," names appearing on early colonial maps of the region. The etymology remains somewhat debated among historians and linguists, but the "meeting place" interpretation is the most widely accepted.

The name was officially announced on **March 12, 1913**, at the foundation ceremony, by **Lady Denman**, wife of the Governor-General.

---

## Design of the City

In **1911**, an international design competition was held, attracting **137 entries** from around the world. The winner was **Walter Burley Griffin**, an American architect from Chicago (who had trained under Frank Lloyd Wright), along with his wife and collaborator **Marion Mahony Griffin**.

Their design featured:
- A **geometric, radial street layout** aligned with natural landscape features (hills, ridges, the river)
- A **central artificial lake** as the focal visual centrepiece
- A **"garden city"** philosophy with abundant parks and green space
- Separation of major precincts (parliamentary, civic, military) along grand axes
- Key triangles connecting Capital Hill, City Hill, and Russell Hill

The result is one of the world's great **planned capital cities**, comparable to Washington D.C. (USA), Brasília (Brazil), Ottawa (Canada), and Naypyidaw (Myanmar).

---

## Foundation and Early Development

| Date | Event |
|------|-------|
| March 12, 1913 | Foundation stones laid; city officially named "Canberra" |
| 1913–1927 | Slow construction, interrupted by WWI and financial constraints |
| May 9, 1927 | Parliament officially moves from Melbourne to Canberra; provisional Parliament House opened by the Duke of York (future King George VI) |
| 1929–1939 | Development further slowed by the Great Depression |
| 1939–1945 | WWII again delays progress |
| 1964 | Lake Burley Griffin completed (Molonglo River dammed) |
| May 9, 1988 | New (permanent) Parliament House opened by Queen Elizabeth II — exactly 61 years after the provisional Parliament House |

---

## Lake Burley Griffin

Central to Canberra's identity is **Lake Burley Griffin**, the artificial lake named after the city's designer. Created by damming the Molonglo River, it was completed in 1964. The lake:
- Covers approximately **664 hectares**
- Features the **Captain Cook Memorial Water Jet**, which shoots water up to **147 metres (482 feet)** into the air
- Is surrounded by most of Canberra's major national institutions

---

## Key National Institutions in Canberra

Because Canberra is the seat of national government and identity, it hosts an extraordinary concentration of important institutions:

**Government & Law:**
- Parliament House (opened 1988)
- Old Parliament House / Museum of Australian Democracy
- High Court of Australia
- Federal Court of Australia
- Numerous federal government departments

**Culture & Knowledge:**
- Australian War Memorial
- National Gallery of Australia
- National Museum of Australia
- National Library of Australia
- National Archives of Australia
- Questacon (National Science and Technology Centre)
- National Portrait Gallery

**Education & Science:**
- Australian National University (ANU) — consistently ranked among the world's top universities
- University of Canberra
- Several other universities and colleges

**Diplomacy:**
- Embassies and High Commissions from over 90 countries

**Commerce:**
- Royal Australian Mint — where all Australian circulating coins are produced

---

## Geography and Climate

- **Location:** Australian Capital Territory (ACT), an enclave within NSW in southeastern Australia
- **Elevation:** ~577 metres (1,893 feet) above sea level — a high inland tableland
- **Distance from Sydney:** ~280 km (~3 hours by road)
- **Distance from Melbourne:** ~650 km (~6–7 hours by road)
- **Climate:** Continental — four distinct seasons. Cold winters (frost common, occasional snow), warm/hot summers. Noticeably different from Australia's coastal cities.

---

## Population

Canberra has a population of approximately **470,000–490,000** (as of the early 2020s), making it:
- Australia's **largest inland city**
- The **8th largest city** in Australia overall
- Smaller than Sydney (~5.3 million) and Melbourne (~5.1 million), but a significant and growing city in its own right

Interesting demographic notes:
- Canberra has the **highest median household income** of any Australian city
- It has the **highest proportion of university-educated residents** of any Australian city
- The economy is heavily oriented toward **federal government employment**, **education**, and a growing **technology sector**

---

## The ACT — More Than Just Canberra

The Australian Capital Territory also includes:
- **Jervis Bay Territory** — a small coastal enclave on the NSW coast, historically granted so that the national capital would have access to the sea/a port
- Various national parks and nature reserves surrounding the city

The ACT has its own elected government — the **ACT Legislative Assembly** — giving it a degree of self-governance, though it remains a territory rather than a state.

---

## Transport Connections

- **Canberra Airport** — handles both domestic and international flights
- **Road network** — well-connected to Sydney and Melbourne via major highways
- **Light Rail** — the Canberra Metro (Stage 1 opened April 2019), connecting the suburb of Gungahlin to the city centre; Stage 2 extensions planned
- No direct rail connection to Sydney on a fast/efficient line (a longstanding political issue in Australia)

---

## Cultural Life

Canberra is sometimes stereotyped by other Australians as a dull "public servant city," but it has a rich cultural calendar:

- **Floriade** — one of the Southern Hemisphere's largest flower/garden festivals, held every spring (September–October)
- **Enlighten Festival** — buildings illuminated with artistic light projections (late summer/early autumn)
- **National Folk Festival** — one of the largest folk music festivals in the Southern Hemisphere
- A thriving arts, restaurant, and café scene, boosted by the high-income, highly educated population

---

## Common Misconceptions — Addressed

| Misconception | Reality |
|---------------|---------|
| "Sydney is the capital" | Sydney is the largest city; Canberra is the capital |
| "Melbourne is the capital" | Melbourne was the *temporary* capital 1901–1927; Canberra replaced it |
| "Canberra was always there" | It was purpose-built; it barely existed before the 20th century |
| "Parliament is in Sydney" | Parliament House is in Canberra |

---

## Summary

**The capital of Australia is Canberra.**

It was chosen as a compromise between the rival cities of Sydney and Melbourne at the time of Australian federation. Designed by American architect Walter Burley Griffin, it is a purpose-built planned city established in the early 20th century. It sits within the Australian Capital Territory, roughly equidistant (as a compromise) between Sydney and Melbourne. It is the seat of Australia's federal parliament, government, judiciary, and national cultural institutions.
